definitions.errors[]: The extractor was run on the bytes and refused: {message, details} are InvalidInput's own attributes. 'synthetic' replaces base64 for the 40 MiB case and says how to rebuild it; sha256/bytes still describe the rebuilt buffer.
definitions.fixtures[name]: base64 is the exact PDF the Node test feeds to the extractor; sha256/bytes describe it; page_count/character_count/empty_pages/metadata/text/page_map/pages are the real PdfExtraction fields. pages[i].fragments carry (x, y, width, height, text) unrounded (compare with a 1e-9 tolerance); diagnostic_row is PdfPage.diagnostic_row().
definitions.fixtures[name].fragment_y_comparable: true only for the 'layout' builder, whose runs are placed with an explicit '1 0 0 1 x y Tm' per fragment so the baseline survives pypdf's TL defect unchanged. false for 'text'/'scanned': those pages break lines with 'T*' + 'TL', and pypdf multiplies the leading by the font size (pypdf/_page.py:1988), so the reported baseline of every line after the first is off by a constant factor — the value is still recorded verbatim, but only its monotonicity is portable.
definitions.fixtures[name].metadata: Exactly the keys the extractor emits (pdf_text._metadata): the builder writes /Title and /Producer and no /Creator, so 'creator' is absent rather than empty. Compare only the keys listed in metadata_comparable.
definitions.fixtures[name].metadata_comparable: The metadata keys a second extractor can be held to. /Title is a UTF-8 byte string that pypdf keeps as bytes (str() then yields Python's bytes repr), which no other reader reproduces, so it is excluded; /Producer is plain ASCII and compares exactly.
definitions.layout.bbox: bbox_for_text(PdfPage built from items+page_box, needle) -> expected (null when there is nothing to match).
definitions.layout.cases[].expected.columns: a direct _detect_columns() call with the page's own tolerances.
definitions.layout.cases[].expected.facts: _LayoutFacts after the extractor's own sequence (_page_layout → _ordered_page_text), i.e. including any reason the rebuild appended.
definitions.layout.cases[].expected.formula: a direct _detect_formula_tokens() call on the normalised text.
definitions.layout.cases[].expected.join_lines: one _join_line() result per line, in _lines order.
definitions.layout.cases[].expected.lines: python _lines(input fragments, LINE_Y_TOLERANCE_PT / page height) with every fragment mapped back to its index in input.items; -1 would mean a fragment the input never had.
definitions.layout.cases[].expected.ordered_text: _ordered_page_text() result — the text a page stores.
definitions.layout.cases[].expected.table_grid: a direct _detect_table_grid() call with the page's own tolerances.
definitions.layout.cases[].expected.x_clusters: same mapping for _x_clusters(..., COLUMN_X_TOLERANCE_PT / page width).
definitions.layout.cases[].input: items are (text, x_pt, y_pt, size): PDF user space, origin bottom-left, y_pt is the baseline, exactly the convention tests/support/pdf_builder.py uses. page_box is the mediabox [left, bottom, right, top]. text is the page text the extractor would have got (row-major, i.e. the content-stream order). 'truncated' mirrors _PageNotes.truncated (the per-page fragment cap was hit).
definitions.layout.page_map: PdfExtraction(page texts).page_map() -> [(page_index, start, end)] code-point offsets.

note: Generated by scripts/gen_ingestion_b4_pdf_golden.py from the real apps.ingestion.services.pdf_text functions and the real tests/support/pdf_builder.py generators. Do not hand-edit.
notes: pypdf TL defect (fixtures with fragment_y_comparable=false): pypdf/_page.py:1988 computes `TL = float(operands[0]) * font_size * scale_x`, but per the PDF spec TL is already in unscaled text space units. Any page that breaks lines with T* + TL — which is how build_text_pdf and build_scanned_pdf place their text — therefore gets every baseline after the first multiplied by the font size: a 5-line build_text_pdf page lays out at 800/786/772/758/744 (14 pt apart) but pypdf reports 800/632/464/296/128 (168 pt = 14 x 12). The fragments below still record pypdf's values verbatim (it is the oracle), so the Node side compares x/y only for builder='layout' and otherwise checks monotonicity of y plus the non-geometric facts.

No `no_geometry` fixture: a page that yields text but no geometry is not reachable from bytes built by tests/support/pdf_builder.py. The builder always emits Tj/TJ runs, so both visitors fire; the only way _extract_page returns text with an empty fragment list is a visitor exception, which cannot be provoked deterministically from a valid PDF. Rather than invent one, the behaviour is pinned on the real function in layout.cases: ordering_geometry_unavailable_is_not_blocking (empty items + text) and, on the document side, by the scanned-only refusal in errors.no_text_layer.

The layout threshold vectors use page_box [0, 0, 512, 512]. 12/595 is not exactly representable, so a 12 pt gutter on a 595 pt page lands on the 'not a gutter' side of `gutter_end - gutter_start < gutter_width` by a fraction of an ulp (measured). 512 makes 12/512, 3/512, 6/512 and 256/512 exact binary fractions, so those vectors test the comparison operators (< vs <=) rather than float rounding.

fixtures[*].metadata.title is Python's repr of the raw byte string ("b'AcePass \\xe6...'"), not decoded text: a /Title written as UTF-8 bytes without a BOM is not valid PDFDocEncoding, so pypdf keeps it as a ByteStringObject and _metadata does str(value). pdfjs decodes the same bytes as mojibake, so the two are not comparable; that is why each fixture lists metadata_comparable (only /Producer) and the title is recorded for documentation, not for equality.

The encrypted fixtures are deterministic because pypdf derives /ID from a checksum of the document structure and RC4-128 key derivation has no salt. The sha256 values are the proof: if a future pypdf salts either, the vectors fail loudly.
errors.too_large carries 'synthetic' instead of base64 (40 MiB of zeros): prefix + '0' * length, sha256 recorded over the reconstruction.

There is no fixture for MAX_FRAGMENTS_PER_PAGE truncation on a real document: it needs 4005 fragments, which would put a ~0.5 MB fragment dump in this file. The flag is pinned through layout.cases ordering_truncated_marks_reading_order_unreliable, which sets _PageNotes.truncated exactly as the visitor does.
Mixed-column ordering uses short one-character runs so the gutter arithmetic stays readable; that is why several column vectors share the same expected ordered_text pattern of 甲 lines.
